Nearly a thousand PhDs wrote in to say this answer was wrong.
Three doors: a car behind one, goats behind the others.
The host knows where the car is, and always opens a goat door you didn't pick.
Should you switch to door two?
Now try a hundred doors. Your pick is a one-in-a-hundred chance.
The host always opens ninety-eight goat doors.
The one door he left shut holds the other ninety-nine chances.
With three doors, switching wins two times out of three.
Marilyn vos Savant was right: always switch.
